violation_type.title: Naptime for Infants (26 TAC §746.2423)
violation_type.typical_finding: An infant was showing noticeable signs being tired and grabbing at the rails of their crib. The caregiver told the child that they know the child is tired but they have at least an hour before they can lay down. The child then began pushing and biting other children due to being tired and requiring rest.

finding_variants.text: An infant was showing noticeable signs being tired and grabbing at the rails of their crib. The caregiver told the child that they know the child is tired but they have at least an hour before they can lay down. The child then began pushing and biting other children due to being tired and requiring rest.

Infants were observed rubbing their eyes and crying during activities prior to meal time. None of them were provided an option to lay down if needed to nap. Staff stated that nap time starts at 11:30 am.

It was observed on camera that a caregiver did not allow an infant to form his/her own pattern of sleep by continuing to lay the infants head down after the infant has woken.   This was corrected, as the caregiver is no longer employed at the operation.

Caregivers attempt to keep infants awake if they appear sleepy outside of the scheduled napping hours. Caregivers have placed cold towels on the child's cheeks or walked them in a stroller to keep them awake.
They was a four month old infant sleeping in the classroom alone with the lights out in the classroom.
An infant was observed falling asleep in the classroom and the caregiver woke up the infant and told the infant that they couldn't nap at that time.
